fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responding units locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responding units can distinguish it from the main driveway without delay.
• Post a site map or structure diagram near the driveway entrance showing the locations of both detached structures, the storage area, and the access drive.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles traveling to the rear of the property.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and stored materials so emergency vehicles can reach all structures without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the sides of the main driveway so responding units have a clear line of sight when approaching and exiting.
• Mark any gates along the perimeter fencing with reflective hardware and keep them unlocked or equipped with a Knox-type lock for emergency entry.
• Clear a staging area near the front parking area large enough for emergency vehicles to turn around without having to reverse blind onto the road.
• Trim shrubs or trees that block views of the detached structures from the access drive so responding units can see all buildings on approach.
• Post structure labels on each detached building so responding units can quickly identify and communicate which structure they are working at.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structures clear of obstacles so responders can move between buildings on

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any shrubs that are growing directly next to the house or other structures on the property.
• Thin scattered trees near structures so their branches do not touch or hang over rooflines or walls.
• Cut or mow grass close to the house and any outbuildings to reduce the amount of dry material directly around them.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding structures as open and low as possible by removing grass and shrub growth that has grown up against foundations or walls.
• Maintain clear separation between individual shrubs and trees near structures so fire cannot easily move from one plant to the next toward the building.
